media:group.media:title: Djibouti Flood Simulation video - English
media:group.media:description:
In Djibouti, floods are becoming increasingly frequent and destructive. The water can rise unexpectedly, devastating communities that are not prepared. This flood simulation drill brought together community members and local responders to practice what happens before disaster strikes. The goal wasn't just to test whether early warnings reach people, but to ensure everyone knows how to act when they do. Through the Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems (CREWS) Initiative, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the Djibouti Red Crescent Society are helping communities in Djibouti strengthen preparedness, improve coordination, and turn early warnings into early action.
World Meteorological Organization

entry.title: CREWS Cambodia and Lao People's Democratic Republic Project

media:group.media:title: CREWS Cambodia and Lao People's Democratic Republic Project
media:group.media:description:
The Lower Mekong Basin sustains millions across Cambodia and the Lao People’s Democratic Republic — but climate change is making floods and droughts more frequent and unpredictable.
This video highlights how communities are adapting through stronger early warning systems, giving people time to prepare, protect their homes, and stay safe.
With support from the World Meteorological Organization and the Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems Initiative, these efforts are turning forecasts into action — and helping save lives.
World Meteorological Organization
